Collapse Start/Stop Predictions to One Scored Row per Subject

Source: R/tune_start_stop.R
collapse_start_stop_predictions.Rd

Turns row-level linear predictors of a proportional-hazards model fit to start/stop data into what the yardstick survival metrics need: one right-censored truth per subject, a survival curve per subject in a `.pred` list-column (with Graf censoring weights), and `.pred_time` for `concordance_survival()`. Any yardstick survival `metric_set()` can be called on the result.

Usage

collapse_start_stop_predictions(
  truth,
  subject_id,
  lp,
  truth_train,
  subject_id_train,
  lp_train,
  eval_time = NULL,
  covariates = c("path", "baseline"),
  recurrent = c("error", "first"),
  trunc = 0.05
)

Arguments

truth

A [survival::Surv()] outcome for the assessment rows: `Surv(start, stop, event)`, or `Surv(time, event)`.

subject_id

Subject identifiers of the assessment rows.

lp

Linear predictors of the assessment rows (larger means higher hazard). For a parsnip model, `predict(fit, new_data, type = "linear_pred", increasing = FALSE)`.

truth_train, subject_id_train, lp_train

The same for the analysis rows the model was fit on.

eval_time

Evaluation times. Defaults to deciles of the event times of the analysis subjects.

covariates

`"path"` (default) or `"baseline"`.

recurrent

`"error"` (default) or `"first"`, as in [surv_subject_truth()].

trunc

Lower bound for the censoring probability in the Graf weights.

Value

A tibble with one row per assessment subject: `.subject_id`, `.entry`, `.truth` (right-censored `Surv`), `.pred` (a list of tibbles with `.eval_time`, `.pred_survival` and `.weight_censored`) and `.pred_time`.

Details

Survival is predicted from the Breslow baseline hazard of the analysis (training) rows. With `covariates = "path"` the cumulative hazard is integrated over each subject's start/stop covariate path; with `"baseline"`, only the first interval's covariates are used. This is the scoring that [cv_coxnet()] does inside its resamples.

See also

[fit_resamples_start_stop()], [tune_grid_start_stop()], [surv_subject_truth()], [graf_weights()]

Examples

if (requireNamespace("survival", quietly = TRUE) &&
    requireNamespace("yardstick", quietly = TRUE)) {
  set.seed(1)
  long <- do.call(rbind, lapply(1:60, function(i) {
    k <- sample(1:3, 1)
    stops <- cumsum(stats::runif(k, 2, 6))
    risk <- stats::rnorm(1)
    data.frame(subject_id = i, tstart = c(0, utils::head(stops, -1)), tstop = stops,
               status = c(rep(0, k - 1), stats::rbinom(1, 1, stats::plogis(risk))),
               x1 = risk + stats::rnorm(k, sd = 0.2))
  }))
  train <- long[long$subject_id <= 40, ]
  test <- long[long$subject_id > 40, ]
  fit <- survival::coxph(survival::Surv(tstart, tstop, status) ~ x1, data = train)
  scored <- collapse_start_stop_predictions(
    survival::Surv(test$tstart, test$tstop, test$status), test$subject_id,
    lp = stats::predict(fit, test, type = "lp", reference = "zero"),
    truth_train = survival::Surv(train$tstart, train$tstop, train$status),
    subject_id_train = train$subject_id,
    lp_train = stats::predict(fit, train, type = "lp", reference = "zero")
  )
  yardstick::brier_survival_integrated(scored, truth = .truth, .pred)
  yardstick::concordance_survival(scored, truth = .truth, estimate = .pred_time)
}
#> # A tibble: 1 × 3
#>   .metric              .estimator .estimate
#>   <chr>                <chr>          <dbl>
#> 1 concordance_survival standard       0.568
